name: Las Vegas
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Las Vegas: gaming and hospitality diligence, Nevada entity research, convention-sector and asset work.
hero_lede: Las Vegas is the largest casino gaming market in the United States and a major convention and hospitality centre. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Las Vegas matters, using public records and coordinating investigators licensed by Nevada's Private Investigator's Licensing Board and counsel where local work is required.
intro: The Las Vegas-Henderson-Paradise metropolitan area had about 2.35 million residents in late 2023, according to the US Department of Housing and Urban Development, and has grown steadily since 2020. Its economy is built on gaming, hospitality and conventions: the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority reports about 38.5 million visitors, nearly 6 million convention delegates and some 150,000 hotel rooms based on 2025 data, with Clark County gaming revenue of about $13.7 billion. Leisure and hospitality accounted for roughly 26 to 27 percent of employment in 2023 to 2025, with MGM Resorts, Caesars Entertainment and Wynn Resorts among the largest employers. Transportation, construction, education and professional services make up much of the rest.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Las Vegas because large sums move through a concentrated hospitality and gaming economy, and because Nevada is a popular state for forming business entities. Investors, lenders and suppliers need to understand the people behind casino-adjacent businesses, hospitality operators, event and convention contractors and real estate developers. Litigators need background on parties and witnesses in commercial, construction and employment disputes. Creditors pursue debtors whose assets may sit in Nevada entities or local property. Gaming is closely regulated by the state, and Nevada licenses private investigators, so investigative work must be scoped carefully and carried out through properly licensed professionals.

matters.title: Hospitality and gaming counterparty diligence
matters.text: Suppliers, investors and partners of resorts and casinos need to know who stands behind a business. We research ownership, principals, litigation, regulatory history and adverse media of hospitality operators and casino-adjacent vendors, helping clients identify issues that could affect contracts or gaming-related suitability reviews.

matters.title: Nevada entity and ownership research
matters.text: Many businesses with activities elsewhere use Nevada entities. We trace Nevada filings, officers and managers, registered agents and related entities in other states, and identify where ownership is not disclosed, so clients understand which individuals control a counterparty or hold assets.

matters.title: Convention and event contractor checks
matters.text: Las Vegas hosts millions of convention delegates each year, supported by exhibitors, decorators, staffing firms and promoters. We review the corporate background, litigation, liens and complaint history of these contractors before sponsorships, joint ventures or significant prepayments.

matters.title: Construction and real estate disputes
matters.text: Resort, residential and master-planned development in Southern Nevada generates construction and investment disputes. We assist counsel with developer and contractor histories, related entities, mechanics' liens, prior litigation and witness backgrounds in Clark County and other relevant jurisdictions.

matters.title: Judgment enforcement and asset tracing
matters.text: Creditors pursuing debtors with Las Vegas connections need to locate property, business interests and transfers. We work from Clark County property and court records, Nevada and other state entity filings and UCC records to identify likely assets and connected entities for counsel.

local_context.title: Courts in Las Vegas
local_context.text: State civil and commercial cases arising in Las Vegas are heard by the Eighth Judicial District Court in Clark County, which handles complex business matters through a specialised business docket. Federal cases are heard by the US District Court for the District of Nevada, which sits in Las Vegas and Reno, with appeals to the Ninth Circuit. Counsel decides the forum; we tailor research to the case's needs.

local_context.title: Nevada investigator licensing
local_context.text: Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 648 requires a licence from the Private Investigator's Licensing Board, a five-member board appointed by the Governor, to engage in or advertise the business of private investigator, process server, repossessor, security consultant and related activities. A single act counts as engaging in the business. The board can issue citations and fines of up to $10,000 for repeat violations. TDSC coordinates Nevada-licensed investigators for any local work.

local_context.title: Gaming regulation
local_context.text: Gaming in Nevada is regulated by the state through the Nevada Gaming Control Board and the Nevada Gaming Commission, which license operators and many associated persons and publish monthly revenue figures. Licensing and suitability investigations are conducted by the regulator; private research supports clients' own diligence and does not substitute for regulatory findings or access non-public regulatory files. Clients should obtain gaming counsel advice where a matter touches licensing.

local_context.title: Entity and property records
local_context.text: Nevada business entities are registered with the Nevada Secretary of State, whose records list registered agents and, for many entity types, officers or managers, but generally not owners. Real property records for Las Vegas are maintained by Clark County. Because Nevada filings may disclose little about ultimate control, ownership research often extends to other states, litigation and property records. We state confidence levels accordingly.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Las Vegas and works on Las Vegas matters from Nashville. We first agree the purpose with counsel, whether litigation in the Eighth Judicial District Court or the District of Nevada, diligence on a hospitality or gaming-related counterparty, a construction dispute or judgment enforcement, and scope research accordingly. Sources include Nevada Secretary of State filings, Clark County property and court records, federal dockets, gaming regulators' public announcements, other states' registries and media. We do not access non-public gaming regulatory files. Any surveillance, interviews or process work in Nevada is carried out by professionals licensed under NRS Chapter 648, within the scope we set.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Nevada licence to work in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: Yes. NRS Chapter 648 requires a licence from the Private Investigator's Licensing Board to engage in or advertise private investigation and related services, and even a single act can count. TDSC is not licensed in Nevada and coordinates Nevada-licensed professionals for any local work, with counsel confirming requirements before work begins.

faqs.q: Can you find out who owns a Nevada company?
faqs.a: Nevada filings typically show the registered agent and often officers or managers, but not owners. We combine those filings with records in other states, litigation, property and UCC records, and media to identify likely controlling individuals, and we state the confidence level of each conclusion rather than overstating what the records show.

faqs.q: Can you vet a business seeking to work with a casino resort?
faqs.a: We research the company's ownership, principals, litigation, regulatory and media history to support the client's own diligence. Gaming licensing and suitability decisions are made by the Nevada Gaming Control Board and Nevada Gaming Commission; our research does not replace those processes or access regulators' non-public files.

faqs.q: Which courts handle business disputes in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: State business disputes are heard in the Eighth Judicial District Court in Clark County, which has a business docket for complex commercial matters. Federal cases are heard by the US District Court for the District of Nevada. We tailor research on parties, witnesses and related entities to the court and stage of proceedings.

faqs.q: Can you research convention or event partners in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: Yes. Before sponsorships, deposits or joint ventures, we review an event company's corporate background, principals, litigation, liens, complaints and media coverage, and check related entities in other states. This research helps clients identify financial instability, undisclosed related parties or prior disputes with venues and exhibitors.
